ground_truth: Data generated by scratchpad/practical/_gen_t07.py (seed 20261014). True causal effect of the feature on churn is zero: adoption depends on tenure and activity_before; churn depends on tenure, activity_before and a latent activity decline; decliners among adopters disable the feature; CS calls go to adopters (80%) and to decliners (70%) vs others (10%). Proper comparison (ever-adopted on+disabled vs never, same 365d window, all cs_call, stratified by tenure x activity_before) gives standardized difference about +1.9 pp (no reduction); per-stratum differences: new/low +8.7, new/high -0.1, mid/low +0.1, mid/high +0.3, long/low -0.2, long/high -0.7 pp.

planted.description: Common confounder: customer tenure. Adoption share rises with tenure (new 5-20%, mid 13-40%, long 26-61%) while 365d churn falls with tenure (never-group: new 44%, mid 27%, long 14%). The naive comparison mixes long-tenured adopters with new non-adopters.
planted.detect_if: Executor names tenure_band (customer lifetime) as a confounder affecting both feature adoption and churn, and shows or states that the comparison must be stratified/adjusted by tenure (ideally showing adoption rates and churn rates by tenure band, or that within tenure x activity strata the difference largely disappears).

planted.description: Self-selection into treatment: the feature was enabled mostly by customers who were already active (activity_before=high adopts 2-4x more often within each tenure band), and high prior activity independently lowers churn. Within tenure x activity_before strata, adopters and non-adopters (ever-adopted vs never, same window) have practically equal churn.
planted.detect_if: Executor points out that adopters were already more active before the feature (activity_before) and that this pre-existing engagement, not the feature, explains lower churn; ideally shows the within-stratum (tenure x activity_before) comparison with near-zero difference.

planted.description: Reverse causality / misclassification of disablers: feature_status is measured at end of period, so customers who enabled the feature and then turned it off after their activity dropped (feature_status=disabled, 365d churn 59.5%) are put into the comparison group. feature_disable_log.csv shows activity_drop_day < feature_disabled_day for all 60 events and 39/60 later churned: declining activity leads to disabling, not the other way round.
planted.detect_if: Executor notes that the 'disabled' customers are counted in the control group and/or that status is taken at period end, and uses feature_disable_log.csv (or the logic) to argue activity drops before disabling, i.e. impending churn causes turning the feature off (reverse causality); suggests intention-to-treat grouping (on+disabled vs never) or defining treatment at baseline.

planted.description: Different observation windows: in analysis.py the treated group's churn is churned_180d (since enabling) while the control group's churn is churned_365d (whole year). Same-window comparison on the analyst's own sample gives 14.7% vs 51.5% rather than 8.0% vs 51.5%.
planted.detect_if: Executor explicitly notices that treated churn uses churned_180d and control uses churned_365d (or 'period since enabling' vs 'reporting year') and says the rates are not comparable / recomputes with the same window.

planted.description: Conditioning on a collider / post-treatment selection: the analysis is restricted to cs_call=1. CS calls are triggered both by enabling the feature and by signs of churn risk, so among called customers the non-adopters are disproportionately at-risk. Control churn (365d) is 51.5% among called vs 27.1% among not called; on the full eligible base the 365d comparison is 14.6% vs 32.3%.
planted.detect_if: Executor identifies the cs_call=1 filter as a selection on a variable influenced by both treatment and churn risk (collider / post-treatment / selection bias) and shows the control churn differs sharply between called and not-called customers or recomputes without the filter.

planted.description: Causal language and extrapolation from a single observational association: 'снижает отток на 84 %', 'включение всем сократит отток в шесть раз', 'заложить в финплан' rest on one raw difference and a correlation of -0.49; non-overlapping CIs are presented as proof of an effect. No randomization, no adjustment, no counterfactual design.
planted.detect_if: Executor states that the observational correlation/significant difference does not justify the causal claim 'снижает' nor the forecast for the whole base/financial plan, and recommends a causal design (A/B test / randomized rollout, or at least adjusted analysis with explicit assumptions) before the default-on decision.

decoys.description: Exclusion of trial customers (tenure_band=trial) from the analysis.
decoys.why_correct: In the data trial customers have only feature_status=never: the feature is unavailable there (positivity violation). Excluding a population that cannot receive treatment is the correct way to define the target population; it is not cherry-picking. Flagging it as a defect is a false positive.

decoys.description: Use of Wilson 95% confidence intervals for churn proportions instead of the usual normal (Wald) approximation.
decoys.why_correct: The Wilson interval is a standard, better-calibrated interval for binomial proportions, especially far from 50%; the implementation in analysis.py is the correct formula. The problem with the analysis is bias, not the interval method; calling Wilson CIs wrong is a false positive (pointing out that CIs do not address bias is fine).

grading_notes: Единая схема оценки для всех задач: найден=1 (по detect_if), частично=0.5 (названа верная область или симптом, но нет конкретного механизма или выполнена только половина условия), не найден=0. Утверждение исполнителя 'на цифру это почти не влияет' о найденном дефекте ошибкой не считается.
P3 минимум для засчёта: выключившие функцию отнесены к контролю И падение активности предшествует отключению (по журналу). Предложение группировать по намерению лечить желательно, но не обязательно.
Исполнитель, заметивший возможный вред для новых клиентов с низкой активностью, баллов не теряет: это не ложное срабатывание.
